subject: MAP: Embeddings + Reranker load testing — plan, metrics, and close timeline
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: MAP: Embeddings + Reranker load testing — plan, metrics, and close timeline

Alice,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Per our mutual action plan (MAP) I wanted to capture the proposed performance evaluation plan and a suggested close timeline so we can align internal teams and your DevOps. High level goals:

- Validate embeddings endpoint at target QPS and reranker endpoint under concurrent load.
- Measure latency (P50/P95/P99), TTFT (time-to-first-token), and throughput (requests/sec & tokens/sec) across target concurrency profiles.
- Produce a short report with Prometheus snapshots and reproduce scripts for your platform team.

Summary of proposed test matrix (attached in detail):
- Embeddings endpoint: 64-byte vectors, batch sizes {1,8,32}, concurrency {8,32,64}; target steady-state throughput 400 req/s (batching allowed).
- Reranker endpoint (sequence scoring): typical query length 128 tokens, rerank top-5 candidates per request, concurrency {4,16,32}; target tail latency P95 < 250ms, TTFT < 60ms for interactive use-case.
- Mixed load (embeddings + reranker): 70/30 traffic split, measure end-to-end pipeline latency and isolate CPU/GPU utilization.

Deliverables & timeline (draft):
- 2026-02-19: Redwood executes internal dry-run & shares test scripts.
- 2026-02-20 — 2026-02-21: Joint load window with Acme (3 hours each day).
- 2026-02-22: Redwood delivers formal performance report + artifacts.
- 2026-02-25: Customer sign-off on MAP items / decision to proceed to Dedicated capacity or Hosted configuration.

Please confirm availability for the 3-hour joint windows (we suggested 10:00–13:00 ET both days) and any additional success criteria you want captured in the report. Attaching the full test plan and scripts (v2) for visibility.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior AE — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: acme-map-performance-plan-20260218.pdf, reranker-load-scripts-v2.tar.gz

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmecorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP: Embeddings + Reranker load testing — plan, metrics, and close timeline

Sean —

Thanks for the thorough plan. 10:00–13:00 ET on 20th and 21st both work for us. A couple of clarifications before we start the joint run:

- For reranker TTFT: our UI needs first token within 80ms at P95; we can accept 60ms as ideal target but want P95 <= 80ms as pass/fail.
- Can Redwood provide a lightweight agent (script) so our infra team can run a pre-check on our side before the joint window? We prefer to run the script during off-hours to validate networking and TLS.
- Please include GPU utilization and memory pressure in the report; we have limits on burst capacity on our side.

Also can you include an estimate of unit cost (tokens/sec -> estimated $/1M requests) under the host config so our procurement team has a feel ahead of the vendor call.

I'll loop our procurement lead if we look good after the report.

Regards,
Alice Chen
Sr. Product Manager — Search & Discovery
Acme Corp

On Thu, Feb 19, 2026 at 08:12 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> P.S. we will add a lightweight pre-check script to the repo and share Prom scrapers for your DevOps.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 18:46:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP: Embeddings + Reranker load testing — plan, metrics, and close timeline

Team —

Attached is the consolidated performance report from our joint windows on 20–21 Feb. High-level summary first, then a few notes and asks we should surface to Acme.

High-level results (steady-state, all numbers are median of 3 runs unless noted):

Embeddings endpoint (model: open-embed-2b-quantized):
- Config: batch=8 steady-state, concurrency=32
- Throughput: 420 req/s (90% requests with batch=8)
- Latency: P50=12ms, P95=46ms, P99=140ms
- TTFT: 6ms (first token emitted almost instantly for embeddings)
- GPU util: 65% avg, memory 11.5GB used of 16GB

Reranker endpoint (model: rerank-large-1.0, scoring-only path):
- Config: single-request rerank top-5, concurrency profiles tested: 4, 16, 32
- Concurrency=16 (closest to Acme interactive load):
  - Throughput: 72 req/s
  - Latency: P50=38ms, P95=210ms, P99=450ms
  - TTFT: 48ms
  - GPU util: 78% avg, occasional spikes to 92% during P99 events

Mixed load (70% embeddings / 30% reranker):
- Observed end-to-end median latency: 65ms (embeddings + reranker combined, excluding client-side serialization)
- Interference observed when both endpoints saturated: reranker P95 regresses ~25% if embeddings consume >80% GPU cycles; mitigations: scheduling limits + soft quota on batch size for embeddings.

Cost & sizing notes:
- Approx unit cost (hosted estimate using current pricing model): embeddings ~ $0.07 per 10k requests at the tested batch rates; reranker ~ $0.42 per 10k requests (scoring-only path). These are estimates to be refined with actual sustained throughput contracts.

Action items for MAP close / customer communication:
- Confirm Acme acceptance criteria: reranker P95 <= 80ms (Alice requested) — we achieved 210ms at concurrency 16, so we need clarifying: their UI target likely expects a cached/optimized rerank path or model variant. Suggest two options: (A) route interactive traffic to a smaller quantized reranker model to meet P95 80ms; (B) increase dedicated capacity/GPU class to reduce P95.
- Provide a recommended config and cost delta for both options.
- Share artifacts: prometheus snapshots, raw traces, and the scripts (attached).

Attached: acme-map-performance-report-20260218.pdf, prometheus-snapshots-20260218.zip, reranker-load-scripts-v2.tar.gz

Notes: tests run on Redwood-hosted staging with identical vCPU/GPU types to Acme's target nodes; network RTT added artificially to emulate east-coast client 20ms.

Marissa
Principal Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

> On the raw trace P99 spikes: we saw 450ms as a tail — mostly correlated with KV cache misses during long sequences. We added a mitigation note in the report.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP: Embeddings + Reranker load testing — plan, metrics, and close timeline

Alice —

Appreciate the quick cooperation from your DevOps team during the joint windows. To summarize next steps and options so procurement and product can evaluate:

1) Short-term (fast path): route interactive UI to a smaller reranker variant we can provision in-hosted with P95 <= 80ms. Estimated monthly incremental cost: +$6.5k. Tradeoff: slight accuracy delta (~3% on re-ranking eval set).

2) Medium-term (preferred for accuracy): Dedicated capacity with same reranker model on an upgraded GPU class; expected P95 ~120–150ms at concurrency 16; estimated incremental monthly cost: +$18k and 2-week provisioning lead-time.

3) Engineering mitigations: enable prefix/KV warming, cap embeddings batch size during peek windows, and route bulk embedding jobs to off-peak windows. These are low effort and can reduce reranker P95 by ~20% in our tests.

If Acme is comfortable with option 1 we can issue a formal amendment to the MAP and produce a pricing addendum for procurement. Otherwise, we'll coordinate to scope Dedicated sizing and SLA.

Would you like us to draft the short amendment (option 1) for review this week? If so, we can aim to have signatures and order form ready before 2026-02-28 to meet your internal procurement window.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

--
Attachments: acme-map-performance-report-20260218.pdf (see above)
